member.name: Model
member.para: A large model against a small one on short probes. Measured on "Paula Monti.m4b" by replaying a real run's own probe windows (2026-08-08): ggml-large-v3-turbo matched the announcement in 4 of 15 windows at 11-22 s where ggml-small matched 14 of 14. On the same book turbo-throughout lost chapters 19 and 21-25 outright while -m small -M turbo found all 25.

member.name: TrailingScan
member.para: The book that lost its last five chapters with nothing to notice. "Paula Monti.m4b" lost chapters 21-25 (2026-08-08) and was written out with 20 marks, no missing-number list and no ".missing-marks" tag, because nothing above chapter 20 existed to notice they were gone. That is what settled the argument for making the trailing scan a default in 0.11.0 rather than opt-in.

member.name: DefaultChapterCount
member.para: The corpus run whose front matter became chapters. The build-328 run turned the years of a Perry Rhodan "Zeittafel" into chapters 3578-3585, which pushed the real chapter 1 below the sequence, split four books into parts that do not exist, cost "Raumschiff Erde" its prologue (a chapter accepted at 0:01:53 closes the before-first-chapter scope the prologue at 0:03:55 needed) and left ".missing-marks" tags naming numbers no book ever had.
The book lengths 200 is set against. Comfortably past the longest book on record here (67) and past the classics that run longest - "The Count of Monte Cristo" has 117.

member.name: EffectiveMaxChapterNumber
member.para: The run that made --max-chapters a term here. "Perry Rhodan Silber-Edition 98 - Die Glaswelt" (build 411, 2026-08-27), a 28-chapter book run under -x 60 with no --max-chapter-number. Chapter 7 came back as "Kapitel C.", a Roman numeral for 100, which the 200 default admitted without hesitation; the number then invented a second part and cost 27 marks their titles (the whole case is under ). The -x 60 on that very command line was already the statement that would have thrown it away - a book whose mark list is bogus above 60 does not have a chapter 100 - and nothing was reading it.

The user's call, 2026-08-27, along with the reverse inference in ImpliedMaxChapters. The allowance is taken as-is rather than discounted by the non-chapter marks: chapters are a subset of marks, so -x n bounds the chapter count at n outright, and a bound that is sound without calibration is worth more here than a tighter one that needs it.
